tasks.short: Read professional publications and identify developments that could change media plans.

steps.what: Find relevant articles through {EMAIL} subscriptions and a {OTHER} publication reader.
Read shortlisted articles and identify useful evidence.

loop.input: Licensed article text and media priorities.
loop.output: Claims, supporting passages, publication dates and relevance tags.
loop.check: Require exact supporting passages and valid source references; the manager reads consequential originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per article; unreadable or unsupported items return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters cannot reliably extract claims and qualifications from varied prose.

steps.what: Write a short evidence note in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Extracted passages, source references and manager annotations.
loop.output: A concise evidence note separating reported findings from possible implications.
loop.check: Every factual claim links to a passage; the manager approves the note before team circulation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure but cannot condense varied findings into readable prose.

steps.what: Decide which developments merit a media test or planning change.

tasks.design: Configure subscriptions and deduplication in {WORKFLOW}, storing permitted source references in {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a cited reading brief; the manager checks important originals and records test recommendations in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subscriptions could collect material, but relevance assessment and useful notes still required reading across inconsistent publications.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing feed rules handle collection; bounded text extraction and cheaper custom integration reduce briefing effort.
tasks.still_hard: Paywalls, reuse rights, weak studies and claims that do not transfer to the company's audience.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which apparent trend matters commercially, and which evidence is too weak to justify a test.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on whether one emerging media format deserves a small test.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less scanning and note writing, with more time for source checking and test design. Budget authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Assess the quality of a published channel-effectiveness study.
reach.learn: Sampling bias, comparison groups and the difference between correlation and causal evidence.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides trend alerts and monitoring, supporting source discovery rather than replacing professional reading.
Cited extraction and briefing are plausible bounded-loop designs; the digest contains no measured case for this task.

assumptions: This baseline follows the document-heavy prior; substantial reading remains valuable professional work.
Initial scope is approved publications and public material, without employee monitoring.
Build ranges cover a small pilot using existing infrastructure, not new publication licences.
unknowns: Which subscriptions permit automated retrieval and internal summarisation.
Whether article text is accessible or only links and abstracts.
Who can authorise a media test and its budget.
research_questions: Does the brief preserve important caveats while reducing reading time?
Which source-selection rules produce useful material without narrowing viewpoint diversity?
new_work: Check citations and consequential original passages.
Maintain subscriptions, relevance rules and access permissions.
Review missed developments and remove low-value sources.

tasks.short: Attend industry and promotional events to learn, build relationships and identify useful follow-up.

steps.what: Compare event agendas against learning and relationship priorities.
Register through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and add attendance details to {CALENDAR}.
Prepare session choices, questions and relevant account context.

loop.input: Event agenda, manager objectives and permitted account context.
loop.output: Suggested sessions, factual background and questions.
loop.check: Check agenda references and access permissions; the attendee selects questions and sessions.
loop.stop: One briefing and one correction; missing context is flagged rather than inferred.
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching free-text session descriptions to learning questions requires interpretation.

steps.what: Attend sessions, discuss ideas and build professional relationships.
Write a debrief and record agreed follow-up actions.

loop.input: Attendee notes and explicitly recorded commitments.
loop.output: Debrief and proposed actions with owners and dates where stated.
loop.check: Trace conclusions to notes; do not invent commitments; attendee approves shared actions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; ambiguous actions remain unassigned for manual resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes need synthesis, while structured action fields alone lose context.

steps.what: Send personal follow-up messages and arrange promised conversations.

tasks.design: Configure registration and calendar handoffs through {WORKFLOW}, using supported {PARTNER_PORTAL} interfaces and an approval before paid registration. Bounded loops prepare briefings and debriefs in {DOCS}, while approved actions enter {PROJECT} and personal follow-up remains with the attendee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event information, account context and handwritten notes were disconnected; attendance itself requires presence and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing registration and calendar features handle logistics, while bounded drafting can organise agendas and attendee notes.
tasks.still_hard: Unsupported registration portals, selecting worthwhile events and turning a promising conversation into a trusted relationship.
tasks.human_edge: Presence, curiosity, reading social cues and making credible personal commitments.

ambition.what: An opt-in post-event expert roundtable for customers interested in one emerging advertising topic.

tasks.altitude: Attendance remains the largest part of the task. Less administration creates room to host a focused expert discussion; spending and commercial authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Organise a small customer roundtable after an industry event.
reach.learn: Accessible scheduling, participant consent, facilitation and practical event logistics.

evidence.claim: Spotler Events supported customer-event registration in a documented DHL eCommerce case; this supports logistics only.
Briefing and debriefing from supplied notes are bounded drafting opportunities, without automating participation.
Collecting event contacts does not by itself establish permission for marketing email.

assumptions: The baseline is an in-person event, consistent with the strong attendance prior.
Notes are supplied by the attendee; recording other people is outside the initial scope.
Registration automation uses supported interfaces; unsupported portals remain manual.
GDPR applies to contact records; marketing follow-up also needs the applicable ePrivacy basis.
unknowns: Which event portals support registration integration.
Who approves attendance fees and travel spending.
Which contact uses and retention periods are permitted.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed tooling.
research_questions: Does preparation improve the quality of conversations and follow-up?
Which registration and note-capture steps are frequent enough to justify integration?
new_work: Check briefing accuracy and debrief commitments.
Handle failed registrations and changed agendas.
Maintain contact permissions and delete unnecessary personal notes.

tasks.short: Set sales goals and incentives, review performance and coach team members.

steps.what: Reconcile {CRM} sales results with targets in {SPREADSHEET}.
Set team and individual goals using business priorities and territory context.
Design incentive rules within pay policy and available budget.
Calculate incentive scenarios and budget exposure in {SPREADSHEET}.
Approve goals and incentive terms after finance and human resources review.
Assess individual performance against goals, context and documented examples.
Discuss results, hear employee context and agree coaching actions.
Finalise the assessment and record coaching actions in {TALENT}.

tasks.design: Configure a factual evidence view from {CRM} and {ERP} in {BI}, with reconciled definitions and restricted access. Deterministic calculations produce incentive scenarios, while {WORKFLOW} routes approvals and {TALENT} captures manager-written assessments and agreed actions; no model scores employees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales definitions and incentive exceptions differed across records, while fair evaluation depended on context absent from the numbers.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and review features can be configured, and small deterministic calculators can replace repeated scenario work.
tasks.still_hard: Fair targets, contested credit, incentive side effects and employee trust. GDPR, employment requirements and consultation under national rules need local assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding circumstances, giving candid feedback and making defensible decisions about people.

ambition.what: A fortnightly decision on temporary territory support when workload and opportunity are uneven.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling evidence and more time coaching and adjusting support. Personnel and pay decision rights remain with existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Agree lead-quality and capacity measures with the sales team.
reach.learn: Lead definitions, territory comparability and how campaign choices affect sales workload.

evidence.claim: Funnel supports standardised marketing data and reporting; this is adjacent evidence for data preparation, not employee evaluation.
Deterministic reconciliation and incentive calculations can assist preparation while leaving employee assessment with managers.
Introducing AI employee evaluation would require a separate EU AI Act assessment; the proposed scope excludes it.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies where the advertising manager directly supervises an advertising-sales or promotional-sales team.
The baseline uses {TALENT} for formal reviews and {SPREADSHEET} to reconcile sales evidence.
No inferred personality, emotion, employee ranking or automated employment decision is introduced.
Consent-and-access ranges include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal procedures may take longer.
Step shares cover the combined management cycle, not a claim that every activity occurs daily.
unknowns: Whether this role actually manages sales staff.
Which national rules and employee representation arrangements apply.
Who approves targets, incentive terms and final assessments.
Which sales-credit rules, contractual terms and correction routes apply.
Whether existing reporting and review features are licensed and accessible.
research_questions: Can the evidence pack reconcile to finance without hiding disputed sales credit?
Do scenario checks expose incentive behaviour that damages customer outcomes?
Which existing review fields can be reused without collecting additional employee data?
new_work: Maintain sales definitions, incentive formulas and exception rules.
Resolve disputed data before it enters a performance discussion.
Review access, retention and employee correction requests.
Check that factual dashboards are not repurposed into unsupported employee rankings.

tasks.short: Develop growth plans for existing advertising accounts and execute business within the client's mandate.

steps.what: Assemble account history, campaign results and contract limits from {CRM}, {ADS} and {CLM}.
Discuss account priorities, constraints and unmet needs with the client.
Choose growth opportunities and define a credible account strategy.
Write the account growth proposal using approved service and campaign material.

loop.input: Manager-selected strategy, approved service facts and cited account evidence.
loop.output: Proposal narrative with evidence references and explicit assumptions.
loop.check: Validate claims against supplied records; exclude invented results, prices and commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot express how a selected strategy addresses varied client needs.

steps.what: Calculate prices, discounts and margin against approved rules in {SPREADSHEET}.
Approve proposal terms, exceptions and permitted negotiating limits.
Present the proposal and agree scope, price and responsibilities with the client.
Place authorised media orders through {ADS} within the client's mandate.
Update the opportunity and hand delivery requirements to the campaign team.

tasks.design: Join account facts from {CRM}, {ADS} and {CLM}, then use a bounded drafting loop to fill an approved proposal template in {DOCS}. Configure price and discount checks in {CRM}, route commercial exceptions through {WORKFLOW}, and submit media orders only after a person verifies the mandate and commitment; confirmed terms populate {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context was scattered, proposal writing was bespoke, and commercial commitments depended on negotiated authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Accessible records, reusable templates and configurable pricing handle the repeatable work; a bounded loop drafts the narrative.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering genuine demand, protecting margin and interpreting unusual mandates. Consent, objections and lawful audience use constrain campaign execution.
tasks.human_edge: Earning trust, choosing a credible growth opportunity and negotiating commitments both sides can deliver.

ambition.what: Small established accounts whose campaign plans expire without a dedicated growth review.

tasks.altitude: The manager can spend more time on discovery and smaller accounts as proposal preparation shrinks. Negotiating and spending limits remain explicit; the change grants no new power to bind a client.

reach.task: Design a measurable channel test for an account growth proposal.
reach.learn: Conversion definitions, test budgets, attribution limits and lawful audience activation.

evidence.claim: Funnel supports standardised channel data and automated reports, supporting account evidence preparation.
HubSpot offers campaign-plan and branded-content generation; this supports drafting capability, not autonomous account strategy.
An objection to direct marketing also covers related profiling and must stop that processing.
Rule-based pricing, mandate checks and approved-order handoffs are proposed implementation patterns without a task-specific case in the digest.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to an advertising account-service setting with authority to arrange media business.
The baseline uses {SPREADSHEET} for pricing and {EMAIL} for commercial approval between systems.
Client mandates and agreed terms are recorded as structured fields; ambiguous documents receive manual interpretation.
The build covers one proposal format and one supported media-order interface.
GDPR and applicable ePrivacy rules apply; relevant EU AI Act transparency duties must be checked if synthetic advertising is added.
unknowns: Whether this role may transact for clients or only recommend services.
Which mandate limits, approval thresholds and signature requirements apply.
Whether pricing rules and delivery costs are maintained reliably.
Which external ordering interfaces support duplicate prevention and confirmation retrieval.
Which audience permissions and objection records govern each account.
research_questions: Can every proposed claim and commercial term be traced to an approved source?
Can an uncertain order response be checked before any retry risks duplicate spend?
Which smaller account segment has enough unmet demand to justify the added service?
new_work: Review proposal claims, assumptions and commercial exceptions.
Maintain price rules, service templates and client mandate fields.
Reconcile media confirmations and handle uncertain or rejected orders.
Check audience permissions and propagate marketing objections.
Monitor whether additional small-account work remains commercially worthwhile.

role.altitude: The role shifts some reading, reconciliation and proposal administration into configured tools and small deterministic services. People retain strategy, coaching, relationships and binding commercial decisions, with more time to test media ideas and support neglected accounts.
reach: Market research analyst: assess evidence before proposing a media test.
Meeting, convention, and event planner: turn event learning into a focused customer discussion.
Marketing manager: connect lead quality and sales capacity.
Search marketing strategist: turn account growth ideas into measurable channel tests.
skills_to_grow: Commercial pricing, mandate checks and negotiation.
Reviewing generated drafts against source evidence.
GDPR, applicable ePrivacy requirements and relevant EU AI Act duties.
role.ambitious_version: Lead a small evidence-led advertising practice that tests promising channels regularly, offers focused expert discussions and gives smaller established accounts a credible growth plan, while preserving personal accountability for people and commercial commitments.
